acceptance: With an unreadable git state, the TDD check still audits acs/cycle<N> and records that its scope narrowed, with the git error.
With a readable git state, nothing new is recorded.
A test drives both cases through the real TDD floor.
fix: When the paths cannot be read, keep the acs/cycle<N> audit and record the narrowing: a signal or a refusal-note line that names the git error. Keep the TDD side fail-open.
source: TDD-floor fix review, architecture-reviewer round 3 MEDIUM-1 (go/internal/core/build_testaudit_check.go:37)
summary: core.TddTestAuditFailures ignores a git error from worktreePathsSince and audits only acs/cycle<N>. The check then covers fewer packages than the Build floor, and nothing records that. The Build floor still catches the missed findings, but the silent narrowing breaks the fail-loudly rule.
title: The TDD test-audit check says when it narrows its scope because git cannot be read
